ansible-galaxy.description: requirements.yml collections are intentionally unpinned; nothing to bump until versions are added.

pytorch-rocm-wheels.description: PyTorch's ROCm wheel index is an HTML listing of .whl links, not a registry any built-in datasource understands. `format: html` turns the links into version candidates; the packageRule below strips the wheel filename down to the version. The index URL carries the ROCm build (rocm7.2), so a ROCm move is a deliberate edit of comfyui_torch_index, never an automatic bump -- ROCm 10 lives on AMD's own index and changes ComfyUI's dynamic-VRAM behaviour (see the role).

customManagers.description: The PyTorch wheels the comfyui role installs. Bare version strings in an Ansible list, so no built-in manager sees them -- the same blind spot that left ollama_version three minors behind (the manager below). The pin IS the install: roles/comfyui passes these as constraints, so a stale pin is a stale venv that nothing reports. Local versions (+rocm7.2) are part of the wheel filename, which is why this uses the custom HTML datasource rather than pypi: PyPI carries the CUDA build of the same package names, and pointing at it would propose a torch that cannot see this GPU.

The ComfyUI release the role checks out. A bare version string like ollama_version, so no built-in manager sees it. ComfyUI ships often and a release can move the node API the pinned custom nodes call -- the role warns that ComfyUI-ToSVG imports SVG from comfy_extras.nodes_images, which upstream keeps only for backward compatibility -- so this is an update to READ before merging, not a routine bump.

The uv version the role installs from Astral's script. Bare version string, same blind spot. comfyui_python_version is deliberately NOT watched: a Python minor bump rebuilds the venv and every wheel in it, which is a deliberate act, not a dependency update.

Container images in compose files, Jinja (.j2) templates, and Ansible *_image vars. Handles the FORGE-70 tag@sha256 form, tag-only images, and digest-only (no-tag) images. Skips values containing Jinja {{ }} or ${ } (unresolvable tags). IMAGE VALUES MUST BE UNQUOTED: the regex is unanchored so it also matches `<something>_image: `, and the match would include an opening quote but not the closing one, so autoReplaceStringTemplate would emit a dangling quote and corrupt the YAML. Quote support was therefore removed from matchStrings on purpose -- a quoted value is now silently unmanaged (safe) rather than rewritten into broken YAML (unsafe). autoReplaceStringTemplate is what lets Renovate PIN a digest onto a tag-only image; without it the pin branch failed on every run for 3+ weeks with 'Digest is not updated / update failure' because currentDigest never participated in the match.

The Renovate ENGINE version passed to renovatebot/github-action as renovate-version. The action's own default is a floating major tag re-pulled every run, so without this pin the tool that rewrites this repo changes build-to-build and a major can arrive inside an unrelated action bump. Kept as a bare semver string (NOT an image ref) -- the pinDigests exception below exists because appending a digest here would make the input invalid.

The Ollama version pinned in the ollama role. It is a bare version string in an Ansible var, not an `image:` line, so neither the container manager above nor any built-in manager saw it -- Ollama sat three minor versions behind (0.30.7 vs 0.33.3) from 2026-06-08 to 2026-09-05 with nothing reporting it. The role comment explains why the pin is load-bearing: an empty value only installs when the binary is MISSING, so the pin IS the update mechanism and a stale pin is a silently stale install. GitHub tags carry a leading `v` the var does not, hence extractVersionTemplate.

The erpnext_version line in the erpnext role's defaults. It is documentation -- the version that runs is the image in files/erpnext-one.yaml, which the container manager above already sees -- but it has to move in the same PR or it becomes a line that says the wrong version. Same depName as the image, so the two land in one branch.

packageRules.description: The custom HTML datasource yields wheel filenames; this pulls the version out of them. Also keeps the torch trio together -- torch, torchvision and torchaudio are released as a set and the role installs them as one constraint file, so a PR bumping one alone would produce a venv PyTorch itself refuses to resolve.
Pin digests for every managed container image — aligns updates to the FORGE-70 tag@sha256 standard (adds a digest to tag-only images on bump).

The renovate-version input is a bare version string, not an image reference — a digest pin would emit '44.24.3@sha256:...' and the action would fail to resolve it. Must come AFTER the pinDigests rule above; later rules win.
Chainguard free-tier images garbage-collect old digests — must stay on :latest, never digest-pinned.

A database or cache engine's major is proposed, never merged by Renovate (no major is; see the rules at the end), and never routine: the new major cannot read the old one's data directory (see the postgres-18 data-dir gotcha). Until 2026-10-04 these were switched off, so a new major was simply never heard of. The note is the warning that merging one is a decision to do the migration.
prBodyNotes: A database or cache engine major. For Postgres this bump is not enough by itself: the same change has to move the data location and name the database for roles/postgres-major, or the data is lost sight of. docs/runbooks/postgres-major-upgrade.md. Redis 8 starts on Redis 7's data as it is. Decide, then merge -- or close it.

packageRules.description: Ollama ships -rc prereleases (e.g. v0.34.0-rc1) between stables. forge-ai runs the GPU inference the agents depend on -- take stables only.

Patch, minor and digest updates merge themselves once CI is green (#1378), for everything Renovate manages -- the database engines, ERPNext, LangFuse, ComfyUI and PyTorch included. A merge changes git and nothing else: it reaches a host on the next fleet update pass (ansible/update.yml), which is run by hand.

A major never merges itself: it waits as a PR for a decision. The branch prefix is how .github/workflows/renovate-notify.yml tells a major from the rest at the moment the PR opens -- labels are added in a later API call and are not in that event -- so the Discord message for a major says it needs deciding. One Postgres or Redis image name is shared by several services, and by default Renovate would put them all in one PR that can only be accepted or refused whole (the first run did: four databases on three versions in one diff). The per-service rules below split those; a service added later needs a rule of its own or its database majors fall back into the shared PR.

The ERPNext stack's MariaDB follows what the Frappe project ships and tests against (11.8 for Frappe 16), so nothing from 12 up is proposed. It moves when the vendored frappe_docker compose files are regenerated from a release that moves it, and this ceiling is raised in the same change. Digest and patch updates inside 11.x still arrive and merge like the rest.
The same for the ERPNext stack's Redis: frappe_docker ships 6.2, so nothing from 7 up is proposed.
A database or cache major for Gitea arrives as its own PR, so it can be decided and migrated by itself.
A database or cache major for NetBox arrives as its own PR, so it can be decided and migrated by itself.
A database or cache major for LangFuse arrives as its own PR, so it can be decided and migrated by itself.

ERPNext's image refs in files/erpnext-one.yaml and erpnext_version move as one PR. Deploying it is an upgrade, not a recreate: the erpnext role backs up, migrates and compares the ledger totals, so a merged update is safe to leave to the fleet update pass. Until 2026-10-04 everything under roles/erpnext was switched off here with nothing behind the exclusion but a sentence, which is how LangFuse fell a major version behind (#1334).

LangFuse's web and worker images are one release and must move together, so they arrive as one PR. Grouping alone does not make that true: on 2026-10-05 worker 4.51.0 was on Docker Hub and web 4.51.0 was not, so the group PR moved the worker alone and merged itself, and the two ran a release apart. The three-day wait gives both images time to be published before either is proposed.
